docs.title: 编写 Action 与 Recipe
docs.text: Action 是一次操作，Recipe 是一组按顺序执行的 Action。两者都使用普通字典/JSON，因此同一份内容 可以交给 Gym 环境、baseline、轨迹回放和提交验证器。

docs.title: Action：提交一个动作
docs.text:
最小 Action 只包含操作名：

{"operation": "terminate"}

带参数的常见例子：

{"operation": "add_solvent", "volume_L": 0.03, "solvent": 1}
{"operation": "heat", "temperature_K": 350.0, "duration_s": 1200.0, "stirring_rpm": 800.0}
{"operation": "measure", "instrument": "final_assay"}

不要凭记忆填写范围。运行时 schema 会告诉你必填字段、单位、上下界和类别选项：

schema = env.unwrapped.action_schema("heat")

docs.title: Recipe：描述一条实验路线
docs.text:
recipe = [
    {"operation": "add_solvent", "volume_L": 0.03, "solvent": 1},
    {"operation": "add_reagent", "amount_mol": 0.012},
    {"operation": "heat", "temperature_K": 350.0, "duration_s": 1200.0},
    {"operation": "measure", "instrument": "final_assay"},
]

Recipe 适合固定 baseline、教程和回放。它只是动作清单，并不提前保证每一步合法：环境仍会结合 当前任务、物料状态、预算和前置条件逐步检查。

docs.title: 动作失败时看哪里
docs.text:
信号 含义 Agent 通常应该做什么 precondition_failed 当前状态还不能执行该操作 补齐前序步骤或换一个合法操作 unsafe / unsafe_by_task_limit 触发环境或任务风险边界 降低强度、缩短时间或改变路线 high_cost 成本超过任务阈值 减少测量或选择更便宜的流程 low_selectivity 当前路线选择性不足 调整条件或先获取信息 constitution_failed 状态账本或守恒检查失败 将运行视为环境/执行失败并保留证据

这些信号是可学习反馈，不是可以忽略的日志。需要查看当前合法动作时，优先使用 available_actions() 和 validate_action()。

与现实设备的边界

Action schema 描述可评测的虚拟实验操作，不等同真实机器人指令。设备驱动、权限、联锁和安全 审批应由独立 adapter 处理。

docs.title: Connect an agent
docs.text: ChemWorld agents choose one typed operation at a time from public task state. The environment keeps hidden world state evaluator-owned, validates every request, records resource use and writes an exact replay trajectory. Start offline before introducing an external model.

docs.title: Minimal custom agent
docs.text:
Subclassing BaseAgent supplies a zero-external-resource manifest. Use only public task information and public history when choosing an action.

from chemworld.agents.base import BaseAgent, HistoryRecord
from chemworld.eval.runner import run_agent


class TutorialAgent(BaseAgent):
    name = "tutorial"

    recipe = (
        {"operation": "add_solvent", "volume_L": 0.030, "solvent": 1},
        {"operation": "add_reagent", "amount_mol": 0.012},
        {"operation": "add_catalyst", "catalyst": 2, "catalyst_amount_mol": 0.0004},
        {"operation": "heat", "target_temperature_K": 350.0, "duration_s": 1200.0,
         "stirring_speed_rpm": 800.0},
        {"operation": "measure", "instrument": "hplc"},
        {"operation": "quench"},
        {"operation": "terminate"},
        {"operation": "measure", "instrument": "final_assay"},
    )

    def act(self, history: list[HistoryRecord]) -> dict[str, object]:
        return dict(self.recipe[len(history)])


run_agent(
    env_id="ChemWorld",
    agent=TutorialAgent(),
    world_split="public-dev",
    budget=8,
    objective="balanced",
    seed=0,
    task_id="reaction-to-assay",
    output_path="runs/tutorial-agent.jsonl",
)

For a capable agent, prefer act_with_context(context) or act_with_public_view(context, public_view). The official runner detects these methods and provides the current legal operations, resource state, observation summaries and lifecycle status without exposing hidden truth.

docs.title: Built-in offline agents
docs.text:
List tasks and run a deterministic connectivity check:

chemworld tasks list
chemworld run --task reaction-to-assay --agent scripted_chemistry --seed 0

Other constructor-free names include random, lhs, greedy, gp_bo, rf_ei, safe_gp_bo, tool_using_llm_stub and llm_replay. Use make_agent(name) from chemworld.eval.runner when composing runs in Python.

docs.title: Live DeepSeek adapter
docs.text:
Keep the key out of source files and shell history:

export DEEPSEEK_API_KEY="..."

from chemworld.agents.live_llm import LiveLLMAgent
from chemworld.eval.runner import run_agent
from chemworld.providers.deepseek import DeepSeekClient

client = DeepSeekClient(model="deepseek-v4-pro", thinking=True)
agent = LiveLLMAgent(client, role_id="public-example")

run_agent(
    env_id="ChemWorld",
    agent=agent,
    world_split="public-dev",
    budget=18,
    objective="balanced",
    seed=0,
    task_id="reaction-to-assay",
    output_path="runs/deepseek-reaction-to-assay.jsonl",
)

Model identity, retries, token use and estimated cost are recorded separately. Provider failure is not silently replaced with another model or a host-generated action.

docs.title: Codex subscription adapter
docs.text:
Install the Codex CLI, complete codex login with a ChatGPT subscription, and construct CodexSubscriptionClient from chemworld.providers.codex_subscription. Pass that client to LiveLLMAgent using the same runner pattern above. Subscription usage has no per-run USD price, so the accounting receipt reports that limitation rather than inventing a cost.

InteractiveCodexExperimentAgent is the advanced path for keeping one Codex context alive across a complete experiment. It requires an explicit isolated workspace and role identifier; see the class docstring and focused tests before using it in a formal comparison.

docs.title: Reproducibility and safety boundary
docs.text:
• Never commit API keys, provider response dumps or private reasoning.
  • Do not compare live-agent scores unless task, seed, model identity, prompt contract and resource limits are fixed.
  • Validate and replay every submitted trajectory before reporting a score.
  • ChemWorld is a software-model environment, not a generator of physical laboratory procedures.
  • The checked-in live-agent evidence is finite qualification evidence, not a claim that one provider or agent is generally superior.

docs.title: Source synchronization
docs.text:
The 21 October update imports committed foundation work through source revision 8dc31912. Uncommitted development changes are outside this snapshot. This is a development source update, not a new PyPI release or a rerun of frozen scientific evidence.

  • Module declarations now drive model codecs, advancement, state ownership and snapshot continuation.
  • Shared time supports finite heterogeneous vessel groups, declared open flow systems, multiple devices, FIFO measurement queues, maintenance and retained equipment state.
  • Native parameter/measurement inputs and finite calibration use public observations.
  • Scientific additions include residual/DAE infrastructure, bounded SPMe/DFN and particle distributions, expanded property/data methods, selected CALPHAD/ChemSage models, and supported SBML/SED-ML experiment contracts. Each retains its documented limits.
  • The new website adds a capability atlas, searchable index, bilingual domain reader and saved-record player.

Repository tests and runnable examples are distributed with their implementations. References to development qualification notes describe their original source context; those research-workspace records are not a new public evidence release. Historical public evidence below remains tied to its original runtime.

Local synchronization checks on Windows/Python 3.11: test collection found 3,468 cases. The focused 710-case run initially passed 708 and failed two archive-import checks before newly synchronized modules were added to Git's packaging selection. After inclusion, both affected checks and the atomic-data archive check passed (3/3); the packaging progress/error-reporting checks passed separately (6/6). The strict bilingual documentation build and all 17 browser checks passed, including five viewport widths, language preservation, observed-only plotting and downloads. These focused checks do not claim a new full-suite or cross-platform qualification.

The October 2026 development snapshot brings the public runtime up to the current ChemWorld foundation. Package metadata is 0.5.0.dev0; this is a source update, not a new frozen benchmark or a PyPI release.

docs.title: What changed
docs.text:
The native session and domain extensions are now available on top of these existing capabilities. See the native guide for execution, state ownership and model-specific examples, and the extension scope for the delivered models and shared-clock scope.

Capability Current public behavior Materials and vessels Create containers, transfer identified samples, select vessels and route material through declared component ports. Component composition Compile compatible capability networks after dependency, state-owner and resource checks; composition reports use component-network and vessel-qualified state owners rather than the old fixed pattern names. Full-process crystallization Retain phase inventories, crystal populations and seed provenance through sampling, filtration, resuspension and repeated crystallization. Recovery excludes charged seed and uses tracked initial reagent charge. Process control Configure finite ramp/hold programs, queue stages, set feedback and pause/resume advancement. Gas pressure and purge have finite mass and energy accounting. Continuous streams Advance finite feed reservoirs, a mixed tank and collected outlets with coupled reaction and thermal dynamics, plus a bounded electrochemical channel. Measurement design Configure NMR, IR and MS scan count, resolution and dilution, then acquire a paid, sample-consuming synthetic spectrum. Particle-size measurements are available in compatible crystallization tasks. Controlled chemistry Use coupled weak-acid/precipitation worlds with or without an aqueous ion-pair intermediate, and registered crystallization population/occlusion and purification interventions. Resources and replay Retain attempted versus committed actions, physical consumption, rejected requests and exactly replayable current-runtime trajectories. Scientific records Reusable document storage, versioned notebooks and public-history access are included; study-specific campaign runners are not distributed.

Operation, component and instrument declarations come from the native module registry; each compiled world and task exposes its compatible subset. Native physical channels retain units while the historical Gym vector is a compatibility projection. Existing classic optimization and optional reinforcement-learning interfaces remain available.

docs.title: Try the current runtime
docs.text:
uv sync --locked --extra dev
uv run --no-sync chemworld tasks list
uv run --no-sync python examples/demo_configurable_spectra.py
uv run --no-sync python examples/demo_minimal_agent.py --output runs/minimal-agent.jsonl
uv run --no-sync chemworld verify --submission runs/minimal-agent.jsonl --tolerance 0
uv run --no-sync chemworld lab --no-browser

Current source checks use uv run --no-sync pytest -q. The targeted suite covers operation failures, resource accounting, exact replay, multi-vessel routing, control, streams, spectra, crystallization and retained historical evidence. Optional external reference checks are reported as skipped when their reference installation is absent. Install/build checks are described in contributing.

The preceding foundation synchronization on Windows AMD64 completed with 466 tests passed and 1 skipped (the optional external IDAES checkout was unavailable), plus Ruff, mypy and the strict bilingual documentation build. Wheel and source-distribution installs were checked independently on Python 3.11.15 and 3.12.10, including all 15 task initializations, packaged resources, Student Lab and exact replay of the offline examples. These are software integration checks, not a new scientific qualification of the historical reports.

The native extension synchronization adds 21 further installed examples, covering 667 committed operations per archive. Wheel and sdist both passed on Windows Python 3.12.10 with ten upstream solver/reference packages absent, alongside the eight surface variants, four equipment-reuse variants, task binding, saved continuation and JSONL replay. The Python 3.11.15 integration first found two failures among 721 cases: an inconsistent temperature fixture and single-phase inventory roundoff. Both were corrected without relaxing assertions; all 147 affected flash, column, concentration, measurement and public-entry checks then passed. The unchanged checks and the follow-up overlap and are not added into a new denominator.

The latest integrated examples exercise seven continuous workflows through Python, Gym, CLI and Agent interfaces, with sequential and keyed detector noise and fresh-process snapshot continuation. Their scope includes a shared heater, three membrane process/rinse cycles, mineral chemistry, competing analyzer jobs, full-reflux distillation, repeated crystallization and binary solid phases. See the workflow guide for commands and model limits.

On Windows Python 3.11.15, the final public selection passed 81/81 checks, including 56 cross-interface histories and replays and 14 fresh-process continuations. Shared-material regressions passed 71/71. This integration found and corrected order-sensitive finite-feed summation during JSON replay; the complete affected selection then ran again from its first case. Independent wheel and sdist checks both passed on Windows Python 3.12.10, each running all seven default-noise workflows and their new-process replays. These overlapping checks are reported separately.

docs.title: Model scope
docs.text: Spectra are calibrated synthetic reporter signals, not predictions of arbitrary molecular structures. Local time remains the default: operating a selected vessel does not advance other vessels. An explicitly configured shared laboratory clock advances all enabled vessels and schedules equipment queues and delayed readings; its supported combinations are listed in the shared laboratory guide. The gas plenum does not dissolve or react with the liquid. The mixed-tank electrical channel is an idealized two-electron model; the separate native battery domain uses a bounded single-particle model. World-noise shift modes can include a simultaneous physical-parameter change; they should not be treated as pure noise interventions.

docs.title: Historical reproduction
docs.text:
The checked-in evidence reports, original manifest and tutorial outputs remain unchanged. They describe their original runtime. The home-page animation also shows a historical trace. Use the pinned notebook links or check out db98e800 before running scripts/verify_release.py. That script verifies the frozen whole tree; it is not a development preflight for current main.

Current chemistry does not reproduce every old numerical outcome. In particular, the original midpoint partition-world comparison still executes and replays, but no longer meets its old divergence threshold. Current tests retain that negative outcome instead of relabelling the historical qualification as current.

docs.title: Synchronization provenance
docs.text: Runtime source was selected from ChemWorld commit 5156c5c137c29c945759f24f13595eef7ef3cda0 (19 October 2026). Public-specific CLI, provider adapters, documentation and frozen-evidence consumers are retained; manuscripts, private evaluation inputs, study runners and provider payloads are not copied. Version metadata, type annotations and public CLI error handling are integrated here. The later native foundation updates include the domain implementations and cross-domain integration delivered on 20 October 2026. Finite feed normalization and accounting use stable summation so JSON key ordering does not change the material packet or its subsequent replay. The extension roadmap distinguishes delivered capabilities from further scientific extensions.

docs.title: Provenance and sanitization
docs.text:
Every compressed report binds its original SHA-256, sanitizer version, public protocol and a digest of removed metadata. Canonical JSON and gzip mtime=0 make repeated sanitization reproducible.

See the complete report map, representative behavior tables and release manifest.

Finite claim boundary

Passing these checks does not establish universal chemical fidelity, general agent intelligence or safe transfer to real laboratory practice.

docs.title: Integration scope and further scientific extensions
docs.text:
Shared time is an explicit session configuration. All enabled vessels then age together, and snapshots retain queued jobs, pending SSA events and unpublished readings. Local time remains the default. Shared mode supports sequential and keyed detector noise, with explicitly authored subsecond wait ranges. It excludes open flow and alternate phase strategies; see the guide for its full scope. The integrated examples exercise seven continuous histories across four interfaces, both noise modes and fresh-process continuation. Wheel/sdist checks run the default-noise examples and their replays outside the checkout.

Further scientific extensions need their own finite equations, parameters and reference cases: electrolyte-resolved battery models, plating/cracking, nonideal concentrated aqueous chemistry, membrane backflow and chemical cleaning, spatial surface kinetics, crystal breakage/agglomeration, non-isothermal hybrid SSA/ODE, and multi-sublattice solids. The implemented SPM, membrane and binary-solid slices are not complete PyBaMM, WaterTAP or CALPHAD equivalents.

docs.title: Reference and reuse practice
docs.text:
Relevant scientific references include Cantera, PyBaMM, Reaktoro, WaterTAP, IDAES, COPASI, RMG-Py, CatMAP and pycalphad.

New models start with explicit equations, operating ranges, ownership and exchange rules. Native implementations share the existing solver/session and are checked against analytical limits, conservation and finite reference cases. A copied data fixture keeps its source and license, such as the Cantera 3.1.0 mechanism under tests/fixtures/mechanisms/. Upstream solver dependencies remain optional. Independent implementation does not remove license obligations on reused code or data.

docs.title: 安装并跑通第一次实验
docs.text: 这一页只做一件事：从空环境走到一条通过回放验证的 ChemWorld 轨迹。第一次运行建议使用 reaction-to-assay，整个过程通常只需要几分钟。

docs.title: 1. 安装项目
docs.text:
需要 Python 3.11 或更高版本。

git clone https://github.com/sunyrain/ChemWorld-Public.git
cd ChemWorld-Public
python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"

确认命令行入口已经安装：

chemworld --help
chemworld tasks list
Windows文档与参考验证

如果 python 被解析成 Microsoft Store 别名，可以直接使用仓库虚拟环境：

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -e ".[dev]"

只有在构建站点或运行扩展物理参考检查时，才需要额外依赖：

python -m pip install -e ".[dev,docs,physchem-ref]"

docs.title: 2. 运行一个完整回合
docs.text:
先让内置 Agent 完成一次实验：

chemworld run --task reaction-to-assay --agent random --seed 0

命令会把 trajectory JSONL 和 manifest 写入 runs/，并在终端打印实际路径。这里的 random Agent 不是性能基线；它只是最短的端到端连通性检查。

docs.title: 3. 验证结果
docs.text:
把上一步输出的轨迹路径代入下面两条命令：

chemworld verify --constitution --submission runs/<trajectory>.jsonl
chemworld evaluate --submission runs/<trajectory>.jsonl
  • verify 检查文件结构、合同摘要、状态守恒和确定性回放。
  • evaluate 从轨迹重新计算结果，不采用提交文件自带的分数。

看到验证通过后，你已经跑通了 ChemWorld 最核心的链路：

任务 → Agent → Action → 环境 → 轨迹 → 回放 → 评分

docs.title: 4. 用 Python 查看环境
docs.text:
import gymnasium as gym
import chemworld  # 注册 ChemWorld 环境

env = gym.make("ChemWorld", task_id="reaction-to-assay", seed=0)
observation, info = env.reset(seed=0)

print(info["task_id"])
print(info["physics_maturity"])
print(env.unwrapped.available_actions())

available_actions() 返回当前状态下真正可执行的操作。它比维护一套固定动作模板更可靠，因为不同 任务、阶段和物料状态会开放不同操作。

docs.title: 5. 手动执行一个 Action
docs.text:
先读取 schema，再在不改变环境状态的情况下校验动作：

schema = env.unwrapped.action_schema("add_reagent")
action = {"operation": "add_reagent", "amount_mol": 0.01}
check = env.unwrapped.validate_action(action)

if check["valid"]:
    observation, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)
else:
    print(check["invalid_reasons"])

无效动作会带回 invalid_reasons 和前置条件提示，方便 Agent 修改后重试。任务允许哪些操作、 仪器、预算与终止方式，以 reset 信息和任务卡为准。

正确处理未测量值

数组里的未测量值是 NaN，写入 JSONL 后是 null。不要把它当成零；读取数值时同时检查 observed_mask 或 observed_keys。

docs.title: 6. 打开可视化实验室
docs.text:
python -m apps.task_lab.server --port 8876

启动后可以打开：

  • Agent Observatory：观看 Agent 的逐步决策、谱图与资源消耗。
  • Student Lab：手动选择操作，观察实验状态变化。

经典算法和本地实验不需要在线模型密钥。Provider 凭据和私有评测配置不属于本公开版本。

docs.title: Limitations and safe interpretation
docs.text:
ChemWorld is a software-model environment for controlled agent research. It is not a protocol generator for physical laboratory work.

  • Qualification covers finite registered tasks, compositions, probes and world forks—not all chemistry.
  • Public observations are generated by the declared software models and instruments; they do not certify experimental fidelity.
  • Tutorial recipes demonstrate interface use. They are not optimized procedures or recommendations for real materials.
  • Exact replay means the software trace is reproducible under the release contract. It does not reproduce laboratory uncertainty.
  • Controlled hidden components are evaluator-owned mechanisms for research design. Agents must not receive direct hidden-state access.

No manuscript files, unpublished results, development matrices, raw provider responses or private evaluator configuration are included in this repository.

For exact release claims, use the Evidence page and scripts/verify_release.py.

docs.title: Finite low-copy worlds
docs.text:
Two synthetic worlds run on the native session and task-36 direct SSA strategy: biochemical_world("reversible") (A↔B) and biochemical_world("enzyme") (E+S→ES, ES→E+S, ES→E+P). These are numerical examples, not fitted biological systems. Synthetic E is N2 and ES is CH2N2O so binding preserves atoms. There is no Michaelis–Menten reduction and no implicit ODE/SSA switch.

Run without a model key or COPASI:

uv run --no-sync python examples/native_biochemical.py
uv run --no-sync pytest tests/test_biochemical_worlds.py tests/test_stochastic_kinetics.py -q

The ordinary add_component action accepts mol units, but every dose must represent an exact integer number of molecules (within floating-point conversion roundoff). Feed index 0/1 is A for reversible, E/S for enzyme. No fractional rounding, carrier addition, thermal control or flow is supported in this slice. Elemental transitions are checked in exact integer atoms, not a macroscopic mol tolerance. The mol ledger remains the sole inventory; counts are a derived view.

molecule_counter reports independent Gaussian-noisy, signed calibrated counts (standard deviation 1 count, unit response per molecule), never event truth. molecule_capture independently selects each solute molecule with probability 0.1, exports selected molecules to instrument waste, and measures them with the same detector noise. It is an idealized molecular capture, not a withdrawn liquid aliquot: carrier volume stays constant. Analysis effort is 1 s on the offline instrument clock, with no reactor evolution. Both reads cost 0.01. Captured truth and sampling RNG remain private. Empty/noisy channels are not silently replaced by latent values. No saturation or unknown-species identification is claimed.

Process seed is declared in the world, detector seed at session reset, and capture uses a separate persisted stream derived from the world seed. Reads do not change the next reaction or capture; actual dosing/capture invalidates a pending event. Snapshots retain all continuations, and material/batch/vessel initialization restores the declared discrete state (including its initial process/capture seeds). Thus repeated resets are deterministic reinitializations, not independent replicates: author a world with a new seed for an independent process replicate. Stationary instrument usage survives material resets. Snapshots contain evaluator truth and are not agent observations.

Optional external-reference block (no default dependency, choose a fresh output):

uv run --no-sync --with python-copasi==4.48.309 python scripts/validate_native_biochemical.py --output /tmp/biochemical-attempt.json

The authoring repository retains the fixed design and 8,288 development endpoints in workstreams/world_foundation/NATIVE_BIOCHEMICAL_ACCEPTANCE.md and NATIVE_BIOCHEMICAL_RESULTS.json. These run outputs are not distributed here; the optional command generates a fresh complete summary. It compares transient/effectively equilibrated binomial moments, finite COPASI endpoint distributions and volume/count-scaled ODE convergence. Finite distribution agreement is not proof of all kinetic regimes or wet-lab predictive validity. A generic molecule counter and synthetic capture are explicit simplifications, not models of a named physical assay.

docs.title: Run the integrated native examples
docs.text:
These are fixed synthetic development workflows, not autonomous model campaigns or fits to real laboratory data. They use the same ChemWorldRuntime, Gym, CLI, transaction system and replay as the individual native domains. No model key or optional chemistry backend is required. Installed entry points ship in the wheel and sdist; no test helpers or repository-only configuration are imported.

From the locked repository environment:

uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_domains --output /tmp/native-domains
uv run --no-sync chemworld verify --submission /tmp/native-domains/heater.jsonl
uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_capabilities --format json

After installing the built wheel in a virtual environment, the equivalent entry is python -m chemworld.examples.native_domains --output /tmp/native-domains. Use --workflow NAME to select one or repeat it to select several. Outputs are actual action/readout trajectories and terminal snapshots, not invented scores.

Workflow What it exercises heater One calibrated finite heater: gas surface reaction → liquid adsorption → thermal SPM battery. The same device moves, not copies. Each vessel retains its own material and elapsed local time. membrane Three process/rinse cycles on finite feed/pump/RO/permeate and wash/waste inventories; fouling persists, with no refill/reset. mineral Carbonate/calcite kinetics, finite acid input, phase-owned transfer, sampling and pH. shared-clock Independent low-copy A/B SSA and deterministic A/B vessel, two competing requests to one offline molecular counter, delayed results and persistent RNG. distillation Finite tray holdup, retained receiver, timed fraction collection, full reflux and reflux change. crystal Seeding, finite cooling/growth, filtration, resuspension, warm redissolution and a second cooling interval. solid Binary demixing → heating → cooling with local equilibrium and native phase readout.

docs.title: Device and time boundaries
docs.text:
reconnect_heater is a zero-physical-time connection action in an explicitly authored local-clock composition. Pause control first; there must be exactly one thermal device in the world and a destination with a compatible native temperature domain. Its identity, calibration and settings are retained; material does not move. Use select_vessel then heat to operate at its new destination. It does not implement robot motion, spatial collision avoidance or general instrument hot plugging. A rejected reconnection follows normal procedure-penalty semantics but does not change material, equipment or physical time.

The shared-clock workflow is different: all enabled vessels age together under item 39's finite scheduler. It does not couple SSA and ODE inside one vessel, and molecular capture is zero-carrier-volume Bernoulli sampling, not a liquid aliquot. Do not interpret repeated resets with the same seeds as independent runs.

Use --noise-mode keyed to select the existing keyed detector primitive. Examples use world/process seed 7 and independent observation seed 12. Each output includes the parsed composition and literal action sequence in a *-recipe.json file. The shared-clock example explicitly declares subsecond waits so a snapshot can retain a busy one-second analyzer and an unexecuted SSA event; it does not shorten the analyzer's physical analysis time.

An authored shared clock uses LabClockSpec(vessel_capacity=4, ...) to allow four independent closed thermal/SSA vessels. The default is two; the explicit integer capacity is 1–64, separate from the finite job queue capacity. The 1-, 2- and 4-vessel paths have direct functional coverage. All declared vessels evolve to the same event endpoint, including unselected vessels. Changing declaration order or selecting another vessel does not choose the numerical assembly order. One physical heater and one offline analyzer serve persistent FIFO requests. A failed slice discards sampling and RNG changes; the existing rejected-action cost/risk penalty remains in history. Open connections beyond declared finite apparatus, multiple devices and same-vessel ODE/SSA mixing remain unsupported.

chemworld.examples.closed_shared_labs.reactive_closed_lab() authors four independent synthetic systems: a thermal A/B reaction, thermal SPM battery, finite adsorption contact and low-copy SSA. phase_closed_lab() combines finite crystal growth with a separate Al/Cu solid specimen. Construct a ChemWorldRuntime(composition=...) with either recipe and use select_vessel, queue_lab_heat, optional queue_lab_measure and wait. Electrical drive is an explicitly authored initial program; these recipes do not add a controller. The one finite heater moves between systems, and each model keeps its own temperature domain. An isothermal battery advances but cannot accept heating. All strategies must explicitly declare shared_clock=True; installing a module alone does not grant this capability. A physical cutoff aligns every system to that actual time and stops the laboratory. These combinations use the existing native equations and synthetic parameters; they do not establish material fits.

chemworld.examples.open_shared_labs.open_shared_lab("transport") combines the finite source–pump/pipe/heat-exchanger–receiver apparatus with a closed thermal bottle. Choose "membrane" for finite RO, retained fouling, wash/waste and a separate bottle. Select the apparatus's reactor, call set_flow_rate, then use wait to advance the complete laboratory. Select bottle and queue_lab_measure to occupy its one offline chromatograph while flow continues. The existing local run_flow action cannot introduce a second clock here.

Each finite apparatus advances once, including its source and collection containers. The configured vessel capacity counts physical containers: three for the transport example and five for the fouling membrane example. A finite source, collection limit or wash exhaustion aligns all systems to the actual stop. Global material, pump work and heat remain in their original ledgers; connected-system references appear in the outcome diagnostics. Extra paths, shared reservoirs, unmodelled loops and overlapping strategy ownership are rejected during compilation. These recipes reuse the original bounded flow, dilute/isothermal membrane and thermal equations.

docs.title: Residual and caloric solver choices
docs.text:
BatterySPMSpec and TransientElectrodeSpec default to numerical_form="residual". Set numerical_form="ode" to select their original ODE path explicitly. The selection is saved with the physical model and survives snapshot restoration. A residual solve failure remains a numerical failure; it does not select another algorithm.

Both paths use the same finite inventories, transport and reaction equations, energy conventions, device bounds and runtime transactions. For SPM, the residual path solves current and voltage constraints together, including constant-current, constant-voltage and finite-source current limits. Nonterminal events locate the limit transitions. Algebraic values appear in solver diagnostics and are recomputed from physical state; they are not another persistent inventory. The planar electrode retains its existing redox, diffusion and double-layer charge model and its isothermal energy scope.

The common backend reduces regular block index-1 residual systems to BDF or Radau. It is not an arbitrary-index DAE solver. Diagnostics identify analytic and finite-difference derivatives separately; the common physical assembly uses an analytic rate matrix and explicit numerical state/time derivatives.

FiniteTransportSpec.caloric_algorithm defaults to "residual", consuming the same liquid enthalpy, analytic heat capacity and apparatus heat capacity. The explicit "brentq" choice remains available. caloric_residual_system also provides native temperature responses to target energy and declared physical parameters. A missing analytic parameter derivative is reported as unavailable. None of these numerical choices expands the underlying synthetic material scope.

docs.title: Capability and validation scope
docs.text:
See the generated module table. Its source is the installed declarations and their scope notes, not a duplicate capability list. Actual numeric domains come from authored physics and device specifications and are narrowed by task permissions. Presence of two modules is not evidence that every coupling between them is supported. Small SPM, dilute 0D RO and finite binary equilibrium are not full PyBaMM, WaterTAP or CALPHAD replacements.

Export the actual bound public action ranges, material connections and installed instrument declarations for a recipe (or a raw composition file):

uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_capabilities --composition /tmp/native-domains/heater-recipe.json

This reports the current task and active vessel at reset; future vessel choices or physical state changes may change availability. It reuses the runtime's public contracts, not a separate hand-maintained range table.

Validation commands:

uv run --no-sync pytest tests/test_native_domains_end_to_end.py -v
uv run --no-sync python scripts/smoke_test_wheel.py --native-foundation-only --output /tmp/native-install.json

The latter builds both distributions and installs each outside the repository using locked default dependencies. It checks absence of optional upstream libraries, runs the seven examples, and verifies each trajectory in another process. This is a local installation test, not a PyPI upload or formal release. No claim is made about platforms not actually tested in the acceptance record.

docs.title: Native physical sessions
docs.text:
These development examples use the installed current runtime, without a model API key or upstream solver. Start with the finite synthetic CO oxidation model below, then use the domain-specific examples in the later sections. Python 3.11 or 3.12 is the validation target.

Public functional checks live under tests/; bounded optional reference runners live under scripts/. The workstreams/world_foundation/ reports cited in this guide identify development records in the authoring repository. Those run outputs are not part of this public source synchronization; the included commands create new comparison results at the output path you choose.

After installing the wheel or sdist in an isolated environment:

python -m chemworld.examples.native_surface_research --bulk --mobile --terminal-assay
python -m chemworld.examples.reuse_native_equipment

In a development checkout, prefix Python commands with uv run --no-sync. The first example feeds finite stocks, heats, measures, routes material and ends the task. --no-surface runs the same apparatus as an inert or bulk-only system; --bulk adds the declared bulk reaction. --mobile attaches a material-borne surface. Without it, the stationary surface remains on its vessel when gas moves.

The second example uses the same heater model in inert, bulk, surface and combined systems. It initializes fresh material in the reactor between two batches and checks that the retained heater keeps its identity and calibration. It also binds one compiled physical world to two tasks: direct termination and termination followed by a required final assay. Their physical response before ending agrees.

docs.title: Use the same session through other entry points
docs.text:
from chemworld.runtime import ChemWorldRuntime
from chemworld.world.surface_world import surface_world_spec

spec = surface_world_spec(terminal_assay=True)
session = ChemWorldRuntime(composition=spec, observation_noise_mode="keyed")
session.reset(seed=12)
result = session.execute({"operation": "add_component", "component": "CO-feed",
                          "amount_mol": 2e-5})
reading = session.execute({"operation": "measure", "instrument": "gas_pressure"})
for channel in reading.observation.channels:
    print(channel.channel_id, channel.value, channel.unit, channel.quality)
session.close()

ChemWorldEnv(composition=spec) provides the Gym reset/step interface over the same runtime. chemworld.eval.runner.run_agent accepts composition=spec.to_dict() for an Agent. Both entry points retain transaction outcomes, physical duration, resource accounting and the native observation in info.

To execute JSON actions from the CLI, save spec.to_dict() as world.json and each action as a separate JSON file, then run:

chemworld render --composition world.json --seed 12 --noise-mode keyed \
  --actions feed.json pressure.json --format json --trajectory run.jsonl \
  --snapshot continuation.json
chemworld verify --submission run.jsonl

The CLI refuses to overwrite an existing trajectory or snapshot. Snapshots and trajectory provenance contain private simulator state/configuration for evaluator continuation and replay; they are not Agent observations. JSON can reorder map keys, so physical replay uses a numerical tolerance (the CLI default is 1e-5), while categorical outcomes must agree. Replay requires the original runtime semantics; current main does not substitute for frozen paper physics.

docs.title: Readings, time and reuse
docs.text:
Native channels own physical values and units, uncertainty, quality, axes and acquisition times. Invalid or unobserved channels are explicit; a valid physical reading need not fit in [0, 1]. The fixed Gym scalar view is a derived compatibility projection. Use info["native_observation"] or session results for the complete channel record. Calling observe() returns cached readings and does not acquire another sample.

In-situ acquisition advances the world through the same physical integrator. Offline analysis keeps its acquisition snapshot and accounts for analysis time separately. A task requiring a final assay first freezes production, then ends after that assay; it does not advance the frozen production vessel again.

session.snapshot().save(path) and ChemWorldRuntime.from_snapshot(SessionSnapshot.load(path)) support private continuation with compatible bindings. session.reset() creates a fresh world. Evaluator-only reset(options={"scope": "material", "vessel_ids": ["reactor"]}) replaces that material while retaining attached stationary equipment and its calibration. Partial initialization retains clocks, budgets and RNG state; it is not a free Agent operation. SessionSnapshot is also exported from chemworld.runtime.

Current private sessions use chemworld-session-v2. Their phase identities and material coordinate order survive sorted JSON, including retained samples; pending events, apparatus queues, RNG and resource events remain part of the same continuation. Configuration comparison uses the installed model codecs. Supply the same domain_modules registry when restoring a local extension; callable names in a saved binding describe installed code and are never imports.

Older v1 sessions require an explicit SessionSnapshot.migrate_v1(payload) call. This converts the encoding only when runtime semantics match and omitted assembly order is unambiguous. Multiple records without saved order require the original ordering information. Restoration still checks the complete execution binding. Older physical-world inputs retain their supported boundary conversions; this does not authorize reinterpretation of frozen session evidence.

docs.title: Model and acceptance boundaries
docs.text:
The gas reaction, five-step surface rates, finite material transfers, shared internal-energy/heat-capacity balance and heater model are executable physics. The tests' injected numerical failure, process failure and invalid readout are interface fixtures, not implemented failure mechanisms. Thermal stopping uses a real event. Property tables and rate parameters are finite synthetic contracts. Surface flow, arbitrary thermodynamics and new electrode kinetics remain outside this foundation slice.

The native acceptance covers fixed native/Gym/CLI/Agent histories, both observation noise modes, direct/assay endings, replay and retained equipment. Installation checks build both archives and run the installed modules outside the checkout, with Cantera absent and model keys removed from the child environment. Reported platform results apply only to actual runs; this is development acceptance, not a formal release or a claim of general chemical validity. See contribution guide for packaging and frozen releases.

docs.title: Properties at the current state
docs.text:
ComponentPropertyPackage.evaluate_state(...) evaluates a pure state; evaluate_property_state(packages, amounts_mol, ...) evaluates a composition. Both use the existing component IDs, declared aliases and CAS identifiers. Supply temperature_K, pressure_Pa, phase and the requested quantities. The report retains units and validity warnings for each property. For example:

from chemworld.physchem.curated_properties import curated_property_package

report = curated_property_package("7732-18-5").evaluate_state(
    temperature_K=400, pressure_Pa=1000, phase="gas",
    quantities=("cp", "enthalpy", "internal_energy", "density"),
)
cp = report.properties["cp"].quantity().to("J/(mol*K)")

Energy values are molar J/mol, heat capacities J/(mol K), volume m³/mol and mass density kg/m³. The default caloric datum is explicitly sensible H=0 at 298.15 K; it supplies no formation enthalpy or absolute entropy. Supply a CaloricReference when another datum is needed. Entropy and chemical potential require an entropy datum. The six curated packages currently supply gas Cp and vapor pressure; their default material phase does not imply liquid Cp or transport data. Missing quantities raise an error.

Gas states default to the ideal-gas closure. An explicit existing CubicEOSSpec selects PR/SRK volume, fugacity, departures and derivatives on the requested gas/liquid root. This is a single-phase evaluation; phase equilibrium belongs to the flash model. Its Cp derivative follows the selected outer root and does not support root-topology changes. validity_policy="warn" or "ignore" can evaluate beyond a correlation range, but this API retains the invalid-domain record under either policy.

Native reactor and equipment consumers can share PropertyPackageThermodynamics with SpeciesCaloricModel data. They obtain U(n,T), Cv and composition derivatives from the same evaluations at the current candidate state. The common integrator owns time and heat accounting; material mixing solves the same U relation for temperature. Accepted states and authored operating intervals must remain inside the declared caloric domain. This additive caloric runtime does not claim a nonideal closed-volume EOS balance. Existing constant-Cv declarations delegate to this evaluation path; the older liquid volumetric-Cp model and fixed-capacity phase plateaus remain explicitly selected models. Variable-caloric phase change requires a flash/latent closure.

Run python -m chemworld.examples.state_property_research in an installed environment for a property query and an actual variable-Cv reactor history. Its temperature dependence is synthetic and retains the original native U datum; it is an interface example rather than new material data. Production evaluation imports no reference backend. The optional physchem-ref tools are used only for the separate same-equation and model-bias checks documented in workstreams/world_foundation/NATIVE_PROPERTY_ACCEPTANCE.md.

docs.title: TP/PH flash and finite phase inventories
docs.text:
VLEPropertyPackage combines existing property packages, explicit gas enthalpy references and a declared liquid activity model. tp_flash(...) updates K from the current liquid and vapor compositions; an optional existing gas EOS updates vapor fugacity and departure enthalpy. Liquid enthalpy is the temperature derivative of the same Psat/activity free energy, sharing the gas datum. ph_flash(..., pressure_Pa=..., enthalpy_J=...) holds total H fixed and solves T. Pure saturation uses an enthalpy lever rule. Missing/vanished phases carry zero inventory. Unreachable H and nonconvergence raise explicitly.

TP returns a state query when no inlet H is supplied; its heat duty is then unavailable. With explicit feed_enthalpy_J, TP reports the heat required to maintain the specified T. PH reports zero added heat and its actual enthalpy residual. It does not close the balance by assigning the residual to a heater.

This first slice supports one liquid plus one gas, two/three components and a convex ideal liquid or certified convex binary Margules liquid. Other activity models and uncertified/nonconvex liquids require the separate LLE/stability solver. Critical transitions and three-phase states are outside this model. The Raoult liquid thermodynamic model neglects liquid volume/Poynting work; its nominal liquid holdup is a separate geometric filling approximation. No exact liquid internal-energy/PV-work balance is claimed.

FlashSystemSpec declares a finite constant-pressure thermal system. A native vapor_liquid_equilibrium component selects its enthalpy strategy through the existing physical advance coordinator. Candidate H is integrated once, PH closes each candidate, and accepted liquid/gas quantities occupy the normal phase ledger. The normal device, feed, material routing, measurement, transaction, resource and snapshot services consume that same inventory. Registered liquid species explicitly declare their carrier representation, preventing a second legacy solvent-volume inventory from being inferred from geometric volume. Element and carrier balance checks remain active.

Run python -m chemworld.examples.native_flash_research for a PH query followed by actual finite feeding, cross-phase heating, a timed phase probe, transfer and termination. phase_state is an explicitly noiseless synthetic sensor, not a claim of experimental phase identification. See workstreams/world_foundation/NATIVE_FLASH_ACCEPTANCE.md for the fixed 27-state thermo comparison and development boundaries.

docs.title: Strict liquid stability and finite washing
docs.text:
liquid_tpd_minimum(activity_model, composition, temperature_K=...) minimizes the actual tangent-plane distance on a deterministic set of simplex starts. equilibrate_liquids(activity_model, amounts_mol, temperature_K=...) minimizes constrained mixing Gibbs energy, refines equality of phase chemical potentials, checks component balances and repeats TPD searches on both resulting phases. A stable feed returns one liquid. A remaining negative post-split TPD rejects an unsupported additional phase. Binary/ternary models support at most two liquids; the finite numerical search is not a proof of exhaustive global optimization for arbitrary activity functions.

mixing_chemical_potentials_RT reports ln(x_i gamma_i), relative to the common pure-liquid standard and divided by RT. Common pure reference terms cancel across equal-T liquid phases; these are not fabricated absolute chemical potentials. Activity coefficients use the existing parameter model, shared with the property and contact calculations.

StrictLiquidSystemSpec declares an isothermal material law, component molar holdups and finite wash policy. A liquid_equilibrium component and matching CompositionPhysics.liquid_models entry enable the normal mix/wash, feed, clock, measurement, material routing and snapshot services. Actual wash liquid comes from a finite named supply; discarded material is an explicit molecular outlet. A miscible wash retains one mixed liquid. Droplet entrainment uses the same inventory transfer function as the empirical contact model. The phase probe reports liquid count and second-liquid fraction as synthetic native channels. Mixing heat and PV work remain explicitly unmodeled in this isothermal slice; no heat-control operation is implied.

The older distribution-coefficient contact model remains a separate model. Its minimum_tpd_like includes an empirical partition drive and is explicitly marked thermodynamic_stability_certified=False. Strict liquid equilibrium does not use that drive or fall back to it after a solver failure.

Run python -m chemworld.examples.native_liquid_research for finite mixing, washing, a timed observation, transfer and termination. The example's Margules parameters and component identities are synthetic. See workstreams/world_foundation/NATIVE_LLE_ACCEPTANCE.md for common-tangent, ternary and actual PhasePy validation.

docs.title: Conservative diffusion primitive
docs.text:
chemworld.physchem.finite_volume provides planar and spherical one-dimensional Fick operators in SI units. DiffusionMesh defines physical volumes and face areas; ConservativeDiffusion.evaluate(amounts_mol) returns molar derivatives and signed face rates without advancing time. Positive prescribed boundary flux means outward flux in mol/(m² s). A spherical center requires symmetry.

operator.couple(existing_inventory_keys, process_id=..., owner_id=..., boundary_enthalpies_J_mol=...) supplies a process and material ports to an existing CoupledSystem. Explicit boundary enthalpies are required for open boundaries. BDF/Radau use the assembled sparse stencil; outward fixed-flux depletion stops at its actual event. The caller retains inventory ownership. This is the shared spatial primitive for subsequent electrode/particle models; these mathematical consumers do not implement a battery or a new PDE runtime.

docs.title: Finite dynamic distillation
docs.text:
DynamicColumnSpec reuses ShortcutColumnSpec for the hardware envelope and VLEPropertyPackage for the thermodynamic law. It has 2–8 equilibrium trays, a finite reboiler, condenser and product collector. Each compartment advances actual component amounts and H; task-18 PH closes its phase allocation at each candidate. Vapor withdrawal and liquid overflow use declared finite holdup laws. Heat and material streams enter one shared BDF advance. This model excludes full tray hydraulics, pressure-drop networks and simultaneous reactions.

A dynamic_distillation component and matching CompositionPhysics.column_models entry select this strategy. dynamic_column_world_spec(spec, initial, ...) constructs a native apparatus from explicitly supplied properties and initial inventories. Real distill, heat/wait and timed observations use the common coordinator; dry, flood, temperature, collection and native vessel-volume boundaries stop at their actual roots. Product history records actual collector increments over time. collect_fraction moves actual liquid n and H into its separate retained phase; it never resets the column or manufactures recovery.

Distill controls are target temperature, duration and finite reflux_ratio. Native event JSON additionally accepts numeric full_reflux: 1 (with the usual required reflux field present); full_reflux: 0 resumes finite collection. The unchanged fixed Gym numeric carrier explicitly rejects this additional field and directs callers to event JSON. The old distillation component remains a labelled shortcut_estimate, without stage histories or a fallback from failed dynamic integration.

PhaseLedger alone owns bulk n. Material and stationary support H occupy separate typed slots. Replacing material retains apparatus heat and device calibration, then equilibrates the new fluid plus retained body through PH. Batch reset uses the declared initial thermal boundary while retaining hardware settings. Snapshots retain all compartments and controls. The synthetic phase probe observes the reboiler compartment. Liquid volume remains the geometric holdup approximation of task 18, with no exact liquid U/PV-work claim.

Run python -m chemworld.examples.native_distillation_research for five actual actions: distill, timed measurement, finite collection, reflux change and stop. The example needs no optional reference packages. Its Cp, latent heat and vapor pressure data are explicitly synthetic. The fixed dynamic grid, IDAES MESH steady comparisons, Fenske limit and time refinement are documented in workstreams/world_foundation/NATIVE_DYNAMIC_DISTILLATION_ACCEPTANCE.md.

docs.title: Finite vacuum concentration
docs.text:
CoupledConcentrationSpec uses the same state-dependent VLE properties and PH closure as flash and distillation. A finite pot and receiving bottle each own component inventory and H. Actual retained pot vapor supplies the withdrawal port. The existing equipment capture fraction routes vapor to the bottle; uncaptured vapor crosses an explicit component/H boundary. Captured vapor remains bottle inventory until PH and the finite cooling port condense it. There is no separate instantaneous condensate calculation or latent-heat debit.

A vacuum_concentration component and matching CompositionPhysics.concentration_models entry select the strategy. concentration_world_spec(spec, initial, ...) constructs a native apparatus. concentrate enables heating and vapor transport. Heat/wait and timed in-situ measurements continue the same physical advance. Heater pause leaves the transport setting unchanged. An operating stop closes transport and heat at its actual root; subsequent passive measurement can cool the bottle. Duration exhaustion with an unmet solvent endpoint is a valid result.

Pot, bottle, condenser gas saturation, residual liquid, target recovery, temperature and vessel volume are finite boundaries. Accepted time, heater delivery, cooling and outlet integrals settle once. Native material receipts authenticate the capture split, component withdrawal and transported enthalpy; reusing an action name does not authorize a new outlet. Numerical failures roll back current material, H and time. PhaseLedger owns all current bulk material; typed material and vessel slots distinguish fluid H from stationary heat capacity. Material replacement retains body heat and calibration, and PH reconciles the fresh charge without advancing time. Snapshots retain actual inventories, controls and cumulative boundary receipts.

An explicitly nonvolatile component uses a liquid Cp/H reference at the model pressure and exactly zero gas allocation. Missing gas properties remain unavailable. The shared RR report retains a trace liquid fraction independently when its vapor fraction rounds to one; the undefined beta=1 objective is null for positive nonvolatile material. This slice supports ideal mixtures with one or two volatile species and an optional nonvolatile target, at fixed pressure, without simultaneous reactions. Liquid volume remains a declared geometric holdup approximation; liquid PV/Poynting work is neglected.

simulate_vacuum_concentration(CoupledConcentrationRequest(...)) and the native operation use the same contribution and common compartment solver. Existing VacuumConcentrationRequest inputs explicitly prescribe a fixed evaluated operating profile. Their differential approximation remains labelled declared_fixed_operating_profile, shares phase-advection and solver utilities, and is never a fallback for a failed native solve. Its legacy service now charges actual elapsed time and delivered heat, including early stops.

Run python -m chemworld.examples.native_concentration_research for concentrate, timed measurement, heater pause, wait and termination. The source/installable example uses synthetic properties and needs no optional reference package. The fixed nine-control grid, two material fixtures, Rayleigh holdup limit and native snapshot continuation are recorded in workstreams/world_foundation/NATIVE_CONCENTRATION_ACCEPTANCE.md.

docs.title: Persistent finite sorbent contact
docs.text:
SorbentKineticsSpec supplies competitive Langmuir affinities, local LDF rates and adsorption energies. Fluid concentration and temperature come from the same candidate used by CoupledSystem; bound molecules enter its inventory once. Temperature-dependent affinity and bulk/bound U offsets must use the same adsorption energy. Carrier heat capacity joins the common temperature balance; no separate adsorption heat is charged. Unequal component mobilities use the documented finite-vacancy uptake constraint to preserve shared sites. This is a zero-dimensional, single-site-class liquid contact with two competing components, without axial bed, pressure-drop or intraparticle resolution.

sorbent_contact components select CompositionPhysics.sorbent_models and the existing coupled thermal strategy. A fixed carrier owns its loading in an equipment slot; a mobile carrier moves actual mass, sites, heat capacity and bound molecules with its material portion. Material replacement retains fixed loading and apparatus heat, mixing fresh material through the common U model. Actual dry/heat/wait advances share one clock and solver. Solver failure rolls back fluid, loading, temperature and physical time; established failed-action cost/risk penalties still apply.

CondensedBackgroundSpec explicitly defines volumetric Cv and U for an L-only carrier, with condensed PV/Poynting work neglected. It does not invent molecular carrier or gas data. A native sorbent fixture must declare a finite carrier source vessel. Existing add_solvent debits that actual stock and transports its energy; routing carries solute U, carrier U and mobile bound material. The static wash source has no active thermal process. Source exhaustion rejects the input, and normal material/batch initialization preserves finite supplies. Explicit entity replacement and new-world reset remain lifecycle boundaries.

The legacy standalone isothermal drying request now delegates to the same instantaneous finite-fluid LDF contribution. It retains an explicit finite fresh bed request and the final spent outlet, without certifying unprovided caloric data. The legacy laboratory runtime owns a 20 g unused-media kit per vessel; each actual dry packet debits it and leaves through an authenticated kg entity receipt. Repeated dry or material reset cannot manufacture fresh media. No second current spent-bed stock is maintained.

Run uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_sorbent_research for eight existing operations through adsorption, finite wash, heating, timed measurement and stop. All constitutive data are explicitly synthetic. The fixed 12-condition contact grid, independent equilibrium references and three native cycles are recorded in workstreams/world_foundation/NATIVE_SORBENT_REGENERATION_ACCEPTANCE.md.

docs.title: Finite transient working electrode
docs.text:
electrode_world_spec() creates a native finite planar O + e ↔ R system. The shared conservative diffusion operator and CoupledSystem advance both species profiles, Butler–Volmer exchange and double-layer charge together. The Robin boundary includes the first half-cell diffusion resistance; the outer boundary is closed. Positive current is anodic. Material and signed charge relations are checked before a candidate is returned for transaction validation. Electrical work is recorded, without claiming complete cell energy closure or counterelectrode chemistry.

from chemworld.runtime import ChemWorldRuntime
from chemworld.world.electrode_world import electrode_world_spec

session = ChemWorldRuntime(composition=electrode_world_spec())
session.reset(seed=7)
session.execute({"operation": "configure_electrical_control", "potential_V": 0.1})
session.execute({"operation": "wait", "duration_s": 5})
reading = session.execute({"operation": "measure", "instrument": "electrical_meter"})
print(reading.observation.native_record())

Set ramp_duration_s on the control action for a linear potential ramp from the current setpoint. Configuration does not advance time; wait and the meter's one-second in-situ acquisition use the same physical coordinator. Measurements expose terminal V and total A, without internal concentrations or interfacial potential. This synthetic meter is noiseless and nonconsuming.

Profiles live once in material phase compartments. Charge and cumulative electrical work belong to the electrode equipment; material reset preserves them, while explicit equipment replacement leaves the actual electrolyte profile intact. Snapshots preserve the control programme, inventories and charge. Static equipment supplies remain separate from moving liquid; dynamic or unsupported material state still requires a compatible advance strategy.

The first model uses constant diffusivities, sufficient supporting electrolyte, isothermal operation and finite series resistance. It excludes migration, convection, homogeneous reactions, current control and full-cell thermal physics. Existing fixed diffusion-layer and RC models remain explicit simpler alternatives sharing the same electrochemical constants and BV factors.

Run uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_electrode_research for three controls, waits and native measurements followed by termination. Fixed numerical checks and development failures are recorded in workstreams/world_foundation/NATIVE_ELECTRODE_ACCEPTANCE.md.

docs.title: Programmed chromatography and persistent instrument state
docs.text:
chemworld.world.chromatography_world.chromatography_world_spec("hplc") (or "gc") creates a finite synthetic three-analyte world with source bottles, a receiver, material routing, waste and one persistent chromatograph. It uses the same runtime, resource ledger, measurement records, snapshots and replay as other native worlds; no model provider or API key is required.

from chemworld.runtime import ChemWorldRuntime
from chemworld.world.chromatography_world import chromatography_world_spec

session = ChemWorldRuntime(composition=chromatography_world_spec("hplc"))
session.reset(seed=12)
session.execute({"operation": "configure_chromatography",
                 "instrument": "programmed_hplc", "program_index": 1})
# Initially the receiver contains blank solvent. Route a finite source aliquot
# into it to measure a standard or sample (see the complete example below).
result = session.execute({"operation": "measure", "instrument": "programmed_hplc"})
print(result.observation.channel("peak_1_area"))

Program 0 is constant (298.15 K, HPLC mobile-phase fraction 0.2); program 1 ramps over 30 s to fraction 0.8 for HPLC or 338.15 K for GC. Program 2 uses knots at 0, 15 and 30 s, reaching 20% of that change at 15 s. These programmes reuse the existing retention equations, with explicit programme delay and a time-integrated elution criterion; the constant case regresses to the existing isocratic/isothermal method. Curves reuse the Gaussian peak basis.

Each acquisition consumes 0.0002 L, costs 0.05 currency and adds 60 s of offline analysis time without evolving the host. Actual analyte residue belongs to an equipment-owned state slot. A blank washes this inventory into the recorded external waste outlet; it is not a reset. Use count, gain/baseline drift, programme and calibration persist through material replacement and snapshot restore. Full reset restores the declared initial instrument.

The public record contains a signal curve, fitted peak areas and concentration estimates with units and quality, plus the declared peak templates and response calibration needed to reproduce the inverse fit without simulator state. This finite instrument assumes known peak identities/shapes; it does not identify an unknown retention mechanism. calibrate_chromatography records the last acquired public peak areas with declared standard_1_M, standard_2_M and standard_3_M; at least three standard acquisitions fit the existing response calibration. It does not inspect hidden concentrations, detector gain or baseline. Saturation, overlap and incomplete elution invalidate estimates, not completed sampling. Re-reading cached observations consumes no sample, time or random draw.

Run the complete standard–sample–blank sequence twice for both instruments and all three programmes, including JSONL replay and independent residue/waste checks:

uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.programmed_chromatography --output /tmp/chromatography-example

Choose a new output directory; existing results are never overwritten. The same module runs from an installed wheel. This is a finite development example, not a fitted real column: three synthetic analytes, symmetric peaks, lumped residue, fixed offline duration and a non-evolving host. Continuous mobile-phase usage, column spatial transport and instrument thermal utilities are not modelled, so no energy-closure or general gradient-column claim is made. See authoring development record NATIVE_CHROMATOGRAPHY_ACCEPTANCE.md.

docs.title: Native single-particle lithium battery
docs.text:
battery_world_spec() installs a finite battery with one spherical particle population per electrode. Each population uses the same conservative diffusion operator as the planar electrode. An internal lithium transfer couples the two surfaces to the applied current; voltage follows the synthetic OCV curves and symmetric Butler–Volmer overpotentials. Current, lithium and delivered electrical work advance in the common solver, with actual surface and voltage cutoff events.

from chemworld.physchem.battery_models import BatterySPMSpec
from chemworld.runtime import ChemWorldRuntime
from chemworld.world.battery_world import battery_world_spec

spec = BatterySPMSpec()
session = ChemWorldRuntime(composition=battery_world_spec(spec))
session.reset(seed=4)
session.execute({"operation": "configure_electrical_control",
                 "current_A": spec.current_at_c_rate(0.5)})
session.execute({"operation": "wait", "duration_s": 600})
reading = session.execute({"operation": "measure", "instrument": "battery_meter"})

The same electrical-control action accepts exactly one supported quantity: current_A or potential_V for this battery, potential_V for the finite working electrode. Both share scalar ramp interpolation and the native meter contract; a source rejects modes and limits it does not support. Positive battery current means discharge. C-rate is defined from the initial usable lithium capacity, not recomputed from subsequent measured capacity. The native meter exposes only terminal V and A. Its one-second acquisition advances the same battery state.

Lithium profiles, signed charge and work belong to the battery equipment and are saved only once. Material reset retains them; replacing the actual battery requires explicit new device state. A surface cutoff preserves the real elapsed time and inventory. Reconfiguring to zero current allows subsequent relaxation. The shared ledger uses positive electrical work into the system, so delivered battery work is recorded with the opposite sign.

The parameters are synthetic and use uniform unresolved electrolyte. The default isothermal option remains available; electrolyte transport remains unresolved, and the optional finite SEI extension is described below. Run uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_battery_research for a discharge/rest/recharge history. PyBaMM is used only by the optional reference block; the ordinary installation runs this example without it. Numerical scope, all development failures and fixed comparisons are recorded in workstreams/world_foundation/NATIVE_BATTERY_SPM_ACCEPTANCE.md.

docs.title: Cycles and a consistent synthetic thermal model
docs.text:
Pass BatterySPMSpec(thermal=BatteryThermalSpec(...)) to evolve temperature. The cell's chemical energy is integrated from the same linear OCV functions, and the common solver balances terminal electrical work, chemical storage, heater input and ambient loss. Kinetic, ohmic and diffusion dissipation are independently derived and checked; they are not added again as reaction heat. The OCV curves have no explicit temperature dependence, so reversible entropy heat is zero. Positive OCV slopes are excluded from this convex thermal model. series_resistance_ohm optionally adds actual voltage drop and Joule heating.

battery_world_spec(spec, thermal_device=ThermalDeviceSpec(...)) attaches the existing heater or isothermal bath. heat, wait and thermal pause/resume use that same device; stirring_speed_rpm is optional on heat. A finite-power heater changes actual temperature gradually. An ideal bath must start at its setpoint and records its actual compensation heat.

Use queue_electrical_stage with exactly one of current_A/potential_V, a finite stage_duration_s, and optionally one native terminal condition: stop_voltage_below_V, stop_voltage_above_V, or stop_abs_current_A. Zero-current stages are rests. Stages append to the source-owned queue; wait advances the common controller, whose interval loop also serves the existing thermal/gas programmes. No battery-specific scheduler is installed. Completed queues switch to zero current. Explicit configure_electrical_control clears the queue and installs a manual step/ramp. Voltage control solves for the current from the actual profile; an unreachable voltage remains at the source current limit, with the actual voltage and limit status recorded.

Each stage transition records the terminal reading and actual elapsed time. Physical cutoff events retain the reached state; numerical failures roll back the complete candidate action, including preceding candidate stages, while retaining diagnostics. Snapshots preserve the queue, cursor, temperature and inventories exactly. Material initialization is an evaluator boundary: it retains battery SOC/profiles and uses the declared initial temperature, recorded in its lifecycle receipt. Continuous cycling uses no such initialization.

Run uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_battery_cycles for two CC/CV/rest/charge cycles. The nine thermal comparisons against optional PyBaMM and two native cycles are documented in workstreams/world_foundation/NATIVE_BATTERY_THERMAL_ACCEPTANCE.md.

docs.title: Finite SEI growth and retained degradation
docs.text:
Add sei=SEISpec() to BatterySPMSpec to enable solvent-diffusion-limited SEI. The explicit total reaction is 2 Li + EC -> Li2CO3 + C2H4, corresponding to two lithium ions and two electrons at the negative interface. EC, carbonate, retained ethylene and both active-lithium profiles live once in the cell's equipment slot. Film thickness and resistance are derived from carbonate stock; there is no independent thickness inventory or per-cycle capacity decrement.

The side current is -2 F r. Negative intercalation carries I + 2 F r, while the positive electrode carries I. Both the particle boundary and negative BV relation use that main current. Film resistance changes measured terminal voltage. Its dissipation and reaction heat use the same chemical state function as the thermal model. The irreversible side process stops at its electrochemical driving-force boundary; high-rate or unfavorable conditions are not silently extrapolated into an endergonic growth regime.

The initial film is explicitly present in the initial elemental inventory. A closed cell consumes its actual finite EC; no hidden solvent reservoir is used. The analytic maintained-solvent check adds a declared external feed instead. Species formulas make Li/C/H/O checks meaningful at the runtime transaction. Material initialization preserves the whole cell's chemical history; replacing the cell uses a new explicit equipment inventory. Snapshot and Agent replay retain film, solvent, gas, active lithium, electrical controls and temperature.

The source queue bounds pending work at 32 stages. Completed stages remain in operation history and are removed from the pending list when new work is added; stage_index remains absolute and stage_offset locates the retained list. Thus repeated finite programmes do not exhaust a lifetime queue limit.

Run uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_battery_degradation for ten continuous native cycles. The synthetic model includes finite solvent, film resistance and the two-electron accounting; it excludes plating, cracking, electrolyte transport and gas-pressure mechanics. Fixed analytic, nine-condition PyBaMM and ten-cycle checks are in workstreams/world_foundation/NATIVE_BATTERY_SEI_ACCEPTANCE.md. Windowed discharge charge and lost-lithium equivalent charge are reported separately: neither is used as a direct substitute for the other.

docs.title: Finite pump, pipe and heat-exchanger transport
docs.text:
transport_world_spec() installs a real finite feed and receiver connected by a bounded pump, pipe and optional Ergun bed resistance. set_flow_rate sets a request in mL/min without advancing time; run_flow or wait advances both inventories together. Zero request stops pumping. run_flow may set the utility temperature through target_temperature_K; otherwise the installed value is used.

The pump solves the greatest flow permitted by the requested rate, pressure head and shaft-power limits. PumpSpec and pump_operating_point accept the connected device's monotone pressure-load law for reuse by a membrane. The example reaches about 12.21 mL/min for a 20 mL/min request and stops at the finite pickup heel without charging the unexecuted time tail.

The common finite-inventory solver advances component amounts and enthalpy. Liquid properties use native packages at the candidate T/x; the exchanger uses the actual mass rate after pump heating. Hydraulic work heats the fluid, shaft inefficiency is explicit external loss, and utility heat uses the existing Nu/U/NTU functions. Source and receiver share pressure and elevation; the pipe/exchanger has negligible holdup and the utility is a declared constant temperature boundary, not an untracked coolant inventory.

Material slots own fluid enthalpy; vessel slots own container heat. The pump owns its specification and control. Default batch initialization preserves the finite feed and its local age. Explicit receiver material replacement retains the actual container heat and recloses temperature without advancing time. Source exhaustion, full receiver and outlet property limits stop the process; numerical failure rolls back the candidate with a diagnostic.

flow_meter reports mL/min, Pa, W, K and L through native channels. Native, Gym, CLI and Agent interfaces share execution, accounting and exact replay. Run uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_liquid_transport. The bounded synthetic model excludes reactions, recirculation, cavitation, two-phase flow and an empirical industrial pump curve. Existing spatial PFR experiments retain their declared geometry model. Validation and optional fluids/ht comparisons are in workstreams/world_foundation/NATIVE_TRANSPORT_ACCEPTANCE.md.

docs.title: Finite crystal growth and dissolution
docs.text:
crystal_thermal components install CompositionPhysics.crystal_models beside an explicit thermal model. Existing seed, cool_crystallize, heat, wait, filter and resuspend operations advance the same finite slurry at its actual temperature. A requested setpoint supplies bounded heating or cooling; it does not allocate dissolved molecules in advance. PhaseLedger owns current bulk molecules. Cohort constituent rows decompose the solid into particle counts, diameters, seed provenance and occluded impurity; they are not additional stock.

The declared van't Hoff curve and finite radial growth/recession law share liquid/solid caloric references. One rate/energy assembler and ODE backend advance material, temperature and utility integrals. Geometry coordinates have units m and mol/mol, reconstructing actual molecular stocks for each candidate. Zero-diameter roots remove hosts and release their actual occluded material. Finite impurity capture tapers only below the serialized inventory resolution (default 1e-8 of total impurity); actual remaining stock and numerical corrections are retained and checked against unchanged independent balances.

Nucleation uses explicit temporal birth quadrature, normally 30 s: actual molecules enter nucleus-size reservoirs and join growing cohorts at interval ends. This finite-resolution approximation has a separate interval-refinement check. There is no aggregation, breakage, polymorph or axial population model. Authored condensed Cv and U require negligible condensed PV work; missing phase calorics remain unavailable. Simultaneous bulk reaction and crystal thermal processes are outside this slice.

The native ideal filter retains all particles, solid target, seed and occluded impurity, and 8% wet mother liquor. Its 480 s advances the same active thermal control. Resuspension stores historical filtrate at its own temperature and mixes declared incoming carrier through U, without instant dissolution. Existing resource cards limit fresh carrier and seed. Material replacement retains apparatus heat; snapshots retain cohorts, controls and resource continuation. Current container transfers require equal temperatures when mixing occupied native crystal compartments. Numerical failure rolls back physical state and time, retaining the established failed-action penalties.

The legacy laboratory slurry also uses the finite radial contribution, with its explicit condensed enthalpy boundary. Its carrier Cp is not relabelled Cv. The legacy 96%/92% mechanical retention approximation remains separate and does not certify a complete native U balance. Quench legacy bulk reactions before slurry thermal holds. The standalone prescribed-temperature crystallization provider remains an explicit reference approximation, not a failed-native-solver fallback.

Run uv run --no-sync python -m chemworld.examples.native_crystal_research for eight operations and 901 s of actual time using synthetic properties and no optional reference library. Fixed contact, birth-refinement and two-cycle coverage and all attempted outcomes are recorded in workstreams/world_foundation/NATIVE_CRYSTAL_THERMAL_ACCEPTANCE.md and its JSON.

docs.title: Finite carbonate water chemistry
docs.text:
aqueous_world_spec installs a declared aqueous_mineral component with actual water, H+/OH-, CO2*, bicarbonate/carbonate, Ca, Na, Cl and finite pure calcite. Molality uses actual remaining water kg; geometric liquid volume is a separate declared holdup. Element, carbon, charge, water dissociation and carbonate mass action close together. Finite calcite may appear or deplete; no balancing ion or mineral reservoir is supplied after the solve. Derived speciation is checked against PhaseLedger before a read and is not another material stock.

The same closure serves add_component from finite neutral solution stocks, wait, aqueous-only sample and the non-destructive aqueous_ph electrode. Sampling retains the separate mineral phase. The existing pH meter model uses hydrogen activity and the session RNG; the older simplified acid/base model remains explicit for historical tasks. Both observation noise schedules support exact snapshots and resource continuation. Invalid inputs and numerical failure preserve physical inventories and time under the existing transaction rules.

This synthetic system is restricted to 298.15 K, low pressure and ionic strength <=.1 mol/kg. Constants are pKw=14, pKa1=6.35, pKa2=10.33, log10 Ksp=-8.48, Davies A=.509/b=.3, neutral gamma=1 and water activity=1. Actual water still participates in the reaction element balance. These equilibrium constants do not provide caloric data, temperature dependence or mineral kinetics. Mineral advection and thermal mixing are outside this slice.
